title: Model onboarding adapter and version-pin exposure schema
creator: Ethan Chu
description: Design and implement an API schema and lightweight adapter layer to publish model onboarding metadata, pinning hints, and runtime performance advisories. The goal is to expose a single, discoverable surface that maps model artifact metadata (weights, quantization, tokenizer version) to runtime capabilities and performance profiles (context_window, recommended_batch_size, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_second, memory_footprint_mb, supported_features). This ticket covers schema design, adapter transformation rules (artifact -> capability envelope), backwards-compatible versioning strategy for profile updates, and the rollout plan for surfacing this data via existing model catalog and runtime endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Schema defined for model capability envelope including: id, model_name, model_version, runtime_compat_versions, context_window, recommended_batching, kv_cache_behavior, streaming_supported, tool_calling_supported, structured_output_formats, latency_profile_p50_p95, throughput_tokens_per_second, memory_estimate_mb, quantization_hint, stability_score
Adapter implemented to transform onboarding manifests into capability envelopes for new and patched models

New endpoints (or extended existing endpoints) return capability envelope and explicit pinning hints: e.g., GET /v1/catalog/models/{model_id}/capabilities and POST /v1/catalog/models/onboard (dry-run) with validation errors
Backward-compatible versioning: changes must be additive; breaking changes require migration path and migration scripts
Docs and SDK examples demonstrating how customers can pin to a model_version and read advisory fields for fallback rules
Integration tests that exercise runtime selection when a pinned version is incompatible with a requested capability (e.g., streaming) and verify fallback path and telemetry emitted
notes: Motivation: customers pinning to versions need deterministic behavior guarantees and visibility into trade-offs (latency vs memory). Current catalog lacks a machine-readable advisory surface for operational routing and cost estimates.

Key design choice: surface both 'guaranteed' capabilities (strictly enforced by runtime) and 'advisory' fields (estimates measured from benchmark harness). Advisory fields will be tagged with provenance and timestamp.
Schema must support multiple performance profiles per model_version (e.g., small-batch/p99-optimized, low-latency config) and provide an ID to reference in rollout and Dedicated capacity policies.
implementation_plan: 1) Finalize capability envelope schema with product and runtime (2 days)
2) Implement adapter service that consumes existing manifest v2 and benchmark outputs -> emits capability envelopes (4 days)
3) Extend catalog API to serve capability envelopes and add pinning-hint fields (3 days)
4) Add runtime checks and fallback rules: when a pinned version lacks feature X, return explicit error or route to fallback variant (5 days)
5) Write integration tests + e2e validation in staging, and add telemetry for pin rejection/fallback events (3 days)
6) Docs, SDK examples, and partner comms (2 days)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Runtime will have incompatible semantics across versions, causing unexpected failures when pinning. Mitigation: add strict compatibility flags, and a validation dry-run endpoint to detect incompatibilities before allowing pinning.
Risk: Performance estimates may be stale or noisy. Mitigation: include provenance + sample-distribution metadata and encourage continuous benchmarking; mark advisory data with confidence levels.
Risk: Schema churn impacts many clients. Mitigation: adopt additive-only changes for v1.x; prepare migration docs and feature flags for opt-in behavior.
links_and_artifacts: Staging dashboard for pin/fallback telemetry: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/pins
